title: Diagnose conversion problems before prescribing fixes
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Which page or flow problem to fix first, found by diagnosis methods that fit the traffic level, with each remedy matched to a diagnosed problem.
business_types: any with a website or booking flow
applies_when: Conversion or purchase is the weak link
Owner wants a page redesign or A/B test
exclusions: Demand or capacity is the binding constraint (fix that first)
required_inputs: Funnel numbers for the page or flow
Access to recent buyers, staff or support logs for diagnosis
evidence_requirements: At least one diagnosis source naming why people stall (user-test notes, buyer 'nearly stopped' answers, exit survey, sales/support/chat objections, recordings) with counts n of N
The page or step and its single goal
Traffic source and awareness stage (from conversion-audit step 1)
Weekly visitors to the page (or unknown)
Number of recent buyers reachable and the consent basis
Who talks to buyers (owner, staff, resellers, support)
Page or step reach (share of eventual buyers or visitors who see it)
Owner funnel numbers for the binding-constraint check
Public sources where the audience talks (for audience research)
missing_data_behavior: No visitor counts: qualitative diagnosis only; no uplift estimate.
Expected survey answers below a usable count (computed): use buyer walkthroughs and hallway tests instead.

decision_branches.if: Traffic too low for a survey or test
decision_branches.then: Walkthroughs with recent buyers, ask what nearly stopped them, become a customer yourself.
Rank by page reach x share of mentions, blockers first (ClimbOS scoring, not the authors').

decision_branches.if: A remedy matches no diagnosed problem

implementation_steps: State the page goal and audience
Code each reason into a problem class with counts
Pick the most frequent or most blocking class
Choose a remedy whose function matches it
Place the counter where and when the objection arises
Measure with the feasible method (BK13-K4); re-diagnose if the signal does not move
Write the question the research must answer
Compute expected responses = eligible visitors x response rate (owner rate if known; the book's ~3% only as a dated placeholder)
Pick 2-3 methods from the branch, cheapest first
List problems with class, evidence count and the page/step where each bites
Compute priority = reach share x mention share (proposed, code); blockers override
Prefer pages most buyers see (book: arteries; zero-traffic pages yield nothing)
Write the decision and the five question slots in own words
Estimate days to reach the response target from the owner's traffic and an assumed response rate
Launch with owner approval; keep it running in background
dependencies: Goal defined (book: optimise for the content's reason to exist)
Owner-confirmed facts for any counter-objection copy
Owner approval for any tool install, survey, recording or customer contact
Consent banner and PII masking before session recording where required
Permission before recording calls (book notes this)
Diagnosis from shared/agents/diagnosis.ts showing conversion or activation is the weak link (or unknown)
Owner permission to add an on-site survey

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: About 3-8 owner hours for 3-5 user tests or buyer calls plus coding
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: Can run a silent task-based test and code objections; ClimbOS drafts scripts and codes notes
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Goal event on the page; otherwise label results unmeasured

metrics: Share of research mentions per problem class (n of N)
Goal conversion or earlier step rate
Repeat-test signal: does the confusion or objection still appear?
New themes per extra session (stop when none)
Share of 'already a customer' answers (screen out)
Signup rate of surveyed vs not-surveyed sessions
guardrails: Reported client uplifts are examples, never forecasts.
Session recording needs consent where the law requires it.
No invented proof, guarantees or urgency
Diagnoses labelled 'likely reason', never as proven cause
Contact customers only on a lawful basis; never cold-email purchased lists
Check terms before analysing customer-to-friend messages (the book flags this)
Do not deceive testers about what is being sold
No profit forecast from hypothetical conversion doubling
Book benchmarks not used as targets
Answers labelled 'prospect, fit unknown' and never pooled with own-customer evidence
No personal data required to answer
Do not place on checkout or signup form
alternatives_when_constrained: No traffic: method marketing, selling face to face or by phone, VOC aggregators
No customers: competitor and adjacent reviews (voc-research)
No analytics: owner tally of enquiries and the questions asked
No traffic and no customers: VOC aggregators plus competitor and adjacent reviews (voc-research)
No owner time: remote unmoderated tests (paid) if budget is approved
No tool access: owner notes of every phone or email question for 2 weeks
No analytics: rank by mention share only and label it
No site edit access: ask 5 recent inquirers the same questions by reply
stop_conditions: Remedy shipped and the same objection still appears in the next 3-5 tests: revisit the diagnosis
Two remedies in a row fail to move the step: check whether the binding constraint is elsewhere (shared/agents/diagnosis.ts)
Stop collecting when two consecutive sessions add no new theme
If expected responses for a survey fall below the needed count within the horizon, switch method
Top problem fixed and the step still underperforms: re-run diagnosis
Constraint shifts to another stage: move work there
Signup rate on survey pages drops vs prior period: move or remove survey
Projected time to target exceeds ~8 weeks: switch to audience research
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Few respondents make the top class unstable
Several problems co-exist; fixing one can surface the next
Self-selected testers are more time-rich and cash-poor than buyers
The researcher's own method-marketing experience is one customer
Mention counts reflect who you asked
Reach unknown without analytics (use owner estimates labelled)
Survey placed on the conversion step and hurting signups

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: every 'fix now' or 'test' item in a conversion audit names the diagnosed problem class and its evidence source with a count; items without one go to 'Later' unless they are observable blockers
proposed: order conversion fixes by blockers first, then comprehension and usability, then persuasion classes, within each by reach x mention share computed in code
proposed: show the profit leverage of a conversion change only as an owner-input scenario in economics code, labelled hypothetical, never as an expected result
proposed: voc-research gets a 'site visitor' pool with its own N, confidence ceiling Medium, never blended with own-customer or competitor pools.

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: recommend a guarantee or other risk reducer only when risk or credibility is among the top diagnosed problems (or the owner asks), matching its type to the concern
proposed: weight barrier evidence from recent buyers above non-buyer price complaints when choosing the first fix, while keeping non-buyer purpose data for fit questions
proposed: do not prioritise CRO over reach when the computed binding constraint is demand

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: when no diagnosis evidence exists, output a diagnosis plan before any persuasion remedies

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: before recommending a survey, compute expected responses in code from the owner's traffic and a stated response rate, and switch method if the needed count is out of reach within the horizon
proposed: before recommending a visitor survey, compute days-to-target from owner traffic and an explicit assumed rate in code; if over 8 weeks, offer audience research instead.

external_requirement.rule: proposed: session recording and heatmap suggestions carry a consent and masking prerequisite where privacy law applies
proposed: installing a survey on the owner's site is an external action requiring owner approval.

reconciliation_note: Feeds BKP-05 (what to test) and BRP-14 (question order and risk).
